name: Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act (Revised 508 Standards)
standard: WCAG 2.0 AA (incorporated by reference in 36 CFR 1194, Appendix C, 702.10.1)

laws.cite: 29 U.S.C. 794d (Section 508, Rehabilitation Act of 1973, as amended 1998)
laws.summary: Federal agencies that develop, procure, maintain or use ICT must make it accessible to employees and members of the public with disabilities, comparable to access for others.

laws.cite: 36 CFR part 1194 (Revised 508 Standards and 255 Guidelines, final rule Jan 18, 2017; correction Jan 22, 2018)
laws.summary: The Access Board's technical standards; public-facing content, official communications, software and non-web documents must meet WCAG 2.0 Level A and AA.
Federal acquisitions of ICT must meet the Section 508 standards unless an exception applies.

laws.cite: 21st Century Integrated Digital Experience Act, Pub. L. 115-336 (2018)
laws.summary: New or redesigned public-facing federal websites and digital services must be accessible under Section 508, work on common mobile devices, and use a secure connection.

policy_docs.title: Section508.gov - IT Accessibility Laws and Policies
U.S. Access Board - Revised 508 Standards and 255 Guidelines
OMB M-24-08 Strengthening Digital Accessibility and the Management of Section 508 (archived White House page)

applies_to: Federal executive agencies (and USPS etc. covered by 794d) for ICT they develop, procure, maintain or use: websites, web apps, software incl. mobile apps, electronic documents, hardware, support documentation. Does not directly bind state/local governments or private firms except through federal contracts and some state laws that adopt 508.

deadlines.what: Compliance date for the Revised 508 Standards (existing ICT that met the old standards is safe-harbored until altered).
21st Century IDEA: 180-day deadline after enactment (Dec 20, 2018) for new/redesigned public sites to meet 508 and mobile requirements (computed from enactment date).

exceptions: Legacy ICT safe harbor: unaltered ICT that complied with the original 2000 508 standards
Incidental to a contract (ICT acquired by a contractor incidental to the work)
ICT functions in maintenance or monitoring spaces
Undue burden or fundamental alteration (must be documented, and alternative means provided)
Best meets (procurement when no fully conforming product is commercially available)
Non-public-facing electronic content that is not an official agency communication (only nine categories of internal content are covered)
requires: WCAG 2.0 Level A and AA for web content, non-web documents and software (with WCAG-to-non-web word substitutions and four criteria excluded for non-web: 2.4.1, 2.4.5, 3.2.3, 3.2.4)
Functional performance criteria (Chapter 3) where WCAG does not apply
Chapter 5 software requirements incl. interoperability with assistive technology and authoring tools
Accessibility Conformance Reports (ACR, usually on the ITI VPAT template) used as market research evidence in procurement
mobile: explicit - native mobile apps are 'software' under E207/Chapter 5 and must meet WCAG 2.0 AA via E207.2; 21st Century IDEA separately requires public sites to be fully functional on common mobile devices.
procurement: FAR 39.2 requires 508 conformance in ICT acquisitions; agencies write 508 requirements into solicitations (GSA ICT Baseline / Accessibility Requirements Tool) and evaluate vendor ACRs/VPATs. 'Best meets' applies when no product fully conforms.
enforcement: Administrative complaints to the agency under its Section 504 complaint procedures; private right of action under 29 U.S.C. 794d(f). GSA and OMB collect annual Section 508 assessment data and report to Congress. No civil penalties.
notes: No Access Board rulemaking to move 508 from WCAG 2.0 to 2.1/2.2 was found as of 2026-09-27; the access-board.gov/ict page shows no pending update. Some vendor blogs claim a 'DOJ final rule effective January 18, 2026' requires federal agencies to meet WCAG 2.2 AA; no primary source supports this and it appears to be an error (Jan 18 is the 2017 508 rule date) - treat as unverified/false. OMB M-24-08 (Dec 2023) is linked by section508.gov only via the archived White House site; whether the current administration has rescinded or replaced it was not verified. Exception list and chapter structure drawn from the standards text summarized on access-board.gov; the nine internal-content categories and the four excluded non-web criteria are from E205/E207.
